provenance.notes: Smallest shape that still distinguishes the two gate halves, the per-head eco_a and the column index.
Batch 2 with three heads: the batch stride is zero at batch 1, so a wrong batch term is invisible without this.
A sequence length that is not a multiple of four, so the scalar route runs.
A single query position: the row is one element wide and the gate is the whole computation.
D = 2, the smallest even projection width, so each gate is a single column.
Projection width D=32, the largest used anywhere in this file, checks GatedRelativePositionBias with num_heads=2 at its largest per-head projection size.
A model-shaped head size of 64 with four heads.
A row wide enough that each invocation streams several elements of it.
Negative eco_a values, which flip the sign of the gate_r term before the offset.
Large projections drive both logistics into their flat tails, where the gate stops depending on the query.
A head size larger than the workgroup, so the staged query row is loaded in several strides.
